pll1d45c6-d1e3509.summary: States that by a figure of speech things that are not properly God's will are called his will: prohibition, precept, counsel, permission, and operation; so Scripture sometimes speaks of God's wills in the plural.
claims: Five things are called God's will figuratively.

pll1d45c6-d1e3521.summary: Cites Ps 110:2, 'exquisite according to all his wills': though God has one will, which is himself, Scripture says 'wills' because 'will' is taken in various ways.
claims: God has one will, though Scripture speaks of 'wills.'

pll1d45c6-d1e3545.summary: Adds that Scripture likewise speaks of God's 'mercies' and 'justices' because of their many effects, though in God mercy and justice are one and the same, the divine ousia.
claims: God's mercy and justice are one, the divine essence.

pll1d45c6-d1e3581.summary: Explains that precept, prohibition, and counsel are each called God's will because they are signs of it, as signs of anger are called anger, though there is no anger in God. This is a figure of speech in which the truth is veiled by a trope.
claims: Precepts are signs of God's will.
God is called angry by signs, not by passion.

pll1d45c6-d1e3593.summary: Notes that 'will' means precept and counsel in 'thy will be done' and 'whoever does the will of my Father,' and much is done against this will.
claims: Much is done against God's will as precept.

pll1d45c6-d1e3623.summary: Cites Augustine, De spiritu et littera: unbelievers act against God's will when they do not believe his Gospel.

pl-l1d45c6.summary: Explains that, by a figure of speech, things that are not properly God's will are called his will: prohibition, precept, counsel, permission, and operation (following Hugh of St Victor). So Scripture speaks of God's 'wills' in the plural (Ps 110:2), as it speaks of his 'mercies' and 'justices,' though in God mercy and justice are one, the divine essence. Precept, prohibition, and counsel are called God's will because they are signs of it, as signs of anger are called anger. 'Thy will be done' and 'whoever does the will of my Father' refer to precept and counsel, against which much is done, as unbelievers act against God's will.
claims: Precept, prohibition, counsel, permission, and operation are called God's will figuratively.
Scripture speaks of God's 'wills' because the word is used for different signs.
In God mercy and justice are one, the divine essence.
Precepts and counsels are signs of God's will, as signs of anger are called anger.
Much is done against God's will in the sense of his precepts.
